source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) The Metacognitive Bottleneck: Japanese Riddles (NazoNazo Benchmark)
finding: Insight-style riddles that cause impasse and need a new view are very hard for LLMs. Reasoning models beat non-reasoning models but stay far below humans.
numbers: 38 LLMs, 201 riddles, 120-item human subset (human n=126, mean 52.9%). Non-reasoning models 7.6%, reasoning models 17.6%. GPT-5 alone fell inside the human 95% CI. Full 201 items: medians 9.42% vs 19.25%; pooled odds ratio 2.29.
limits: Public riddles, contamination risk acknowledged. Observational, no causal test. Parameter count did not predict accuracy; release date did.
agent_relevance: Impasse tasks stay hard even for reasoning models, so a scaffold that detects impasse and forces a new framing has real headroom.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) NazoNazo - verification failure analysis
finding: Models often write the correct answer inside their thinking, then do not commit to it and answer wrongly. This is a failure to recognise the resolution of the impasse, not a failure to generate it.
numbers: Verification failures = 5.23% (Gemini 2.5 Flash Preview) to 39.34% (Grok 4) of incorrect answers. Counts: DeepSeek-R1-0528 48 VF vs 42 correct; Claude Opus 4 35 VF vs 61 correct; Grok 4 48 VF vs 72 correct.
limits: Detected by literal string match of the gold answer in the thought log; can over-count. Only 4 models had usable logs.
agent_relevance: Code can scan the trace for candidate answers and force a held-out check on them (G3). Do not let the model drop a candidate without a test.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) NazoNazo - thought-log language and false insight
finding: Thinking language (English vs Japanese) changed accuracy unevenly. Some traces show confident commitment to a wrong new framing, like false insight in humans.
numbers: Grok-4: Japanese 29.5% (33/112) vs English 48.8% (40/82), Fisher p=0.0071. Claude Opus 4: 36.7% vs 28.7% (p=0.356). DeepSeek-R1-0528 100% Japanese, 23.1%. Gemini Flash: 0/12 Japanese vs 11.7% English.
limits: Qualitative, descriptive analogy to human false aha; not mechanism evidence.
agent_relevance: A reframe is not safe by itself. A new framing needs the same check as the old one; the conflict trigger must be a test, not a feeling of insight.

source: Naeini et al. (2023) Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings (Only Connect Wall)
finding: Models given deliberate red-herring clues fail to regroup. Removing red herrings raises performance a lot, which supports fixation (Einstellung) as the cause. More in-context examples did not help.
numbers: Wall grouping, correct groups of 1976 (humans 1405; 285/494 walls solved). GPT-4 0-shot 239 groups, 6 walls; best 5-shot-class 272 groups (3-shot), 5 walls. GPT-3.5 0-shot 114 groups, 0 walls. OCW-Randomized (fewer herrings): GPT-4 up to 655 groups, 68 walls; OCW-WordNet (no herrings): GPT-4 up to 1926 groups, 471 walls. Connections task: best F1 41-45% vs human 80%.
limits: Counts printed per test split (numbers are group counts on different test sets, not same-N rates). Randomised and WordNet sets also change difficulty beyond red herrings, so the red-herring causal claim is partial. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Misleading cues in the prompt lock the model onto the wrong grouping. Re-cluster after removing the first failed grouping; avoid showing prior failed attempts as examples.

source: Kim et al. (2025) Limitations of LLMs in Clinical Problem-Solving Arising from Inflexible Reasoning (M-ARC)
finding: On medical questions built to break familiar patterns (Einstellung), most LLMs score under 50% and are overconfident. Physicians averaged 66%.
numbers: Human mean 66% (5 physicians, SE 5.3%). Best: Gemini 1.5 Pro 50%, o1 48%. Several models at or below 20% chance. Chain-of-thought prompting following MMLU-Pro code. Brier-score calibration: top models overconfident; smaller models more so.
limits: Small set (100 items), 5 human test takers; authors say the aim is not to predict human competence. Humans also limited by Einstellung.
agent_relevance: When the known pattern is wrong, the model proceeds anyway with high confidence. Conflict must be raised by an external contradiction check, not by model confidence.

source: Kim et al. (2026) Advances in LLM Reasoning Enable Flexibility in Clinical Problem-Solving (mARC follow-up)
finding: Newer reasoning models close the gap on the Einstellung benchmark. They do as well as physicians, and better on items physicians miss.
numbers: Best model Claude 4.1 Opus mean 0.751 (95% CI 0.738-0.763) over 15 runs; physician mean 0.66 (CI 0.55-0.75); no significant difference for Claude 4.1 Opus, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.1, Grok-4-Fast-Reasoning. Human-miss set 20/100 items: human accuracy 36% vs 73% on the rest. Best model decisively correct on 55.0% of those items, decisively wrong 25.0%, indeterminate 20.0%.
limits: Highest reasoning effort used. Same small benchmark; the earlier failure was largely a non-reasoning-model failure.
agent_relevance: Reasoning effort cuts fixation sharply (about 48-50% to about 75%). The scaffold should be tested against a reasoning-model baseline, not a non-reasoning one.

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs
finding: With paired control and trap cases, frontier models diagnose the control correctly, then miss the trap where one key finding flips the diagnosis. More accurate models are not always safer.
numbers: 5,383 paired cases, 49 diseases, 17 LLMs. Bias Trap Rate: Gemini-2.5-Pro 60.90% despite top baseline accuracy; most models 43-54%. Robust accuracy only about 11-12% for typical models.
limits: Table in extracted text is partly garbled; only the Gemini value is read with certainty from text. Authors' own ECR-Agent is compared against.
agent_relevance: A counterfactual pair test (change the one deciding fact, see if the answer changes) is a code-checkable conflict test usable inside the loop.

source: Chen et al. (2026) MedEinst - ECR-Agent ablation
finding: A structured scaffold (causal graph reasoning, evidence audit, memory of validated reasoning paths) cut trap rate. Multi-agent debate and dynamic agent selection did not; they amplified the majority prior.
numbers: Qwen3-32B base: baseline accuracy 40.25%, robust 11.86%, trap rate 43.46%. + causal inference (DCI): 55.49% accuracy, 19.94% robust, 38.32% trap. Full ECR-Agent: 69.49% accuracy, 24.21% robust, 33.75% trap. MDAgent and DyLAN: robust accuracy about 8-10% (DyLAN 6.51 baseline).
limits: Authors' own method on their own benchmark; one base model; no external replication.
agent_relevance: Supports G4: debate among same-model samples reinforces the dominant prior. Evidence audit against the deciding fact is the useful part.

source: Xie et al. (2023/ICLR 2024) Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: LLMs in knowledge conflicts
finding: When context clashes with what the model remembers, models accept the conflicting evidence if it is coherent and the only evidence. They show strong confirmation bias when evidence also contains something consistent with their memory.
numbers: Models tested include ChatGPT, GPT-4, PaLM2, Llama2, Vicuna, Qwen. GPT-4 memorised-answer ratio about 80% on the most popular entities. Evidence order changed answers by over 5% generally and over 30% for PaLM2 and Llama2-7B.
quote: LLMs can be highly receptive to external evidence even when that conflicts with their parametric memory
limits: Counter-memory is LLM-generated; high receptiveness could partly reflect fluent text. Single-turn QA, not reasoning conflict.
agent_relevance: Conflict resolution depends on evidence form: coherent, single-source, order-controlled. Present a failing output as one clear contradiction, in fixed order.

source: Xu et al. (2024) Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey
finding: Splits conflict into context-memory, inter-context and intra-memory types. Lists causes, behaviours and fixes. Conflict detection methods exist and work on narrow benchmarks.
numbers: Survey table: Wang et al. (2023h) conflict detection method reports over 80% F1 on contextual conflict detection; Pan et al. (2023b) mitigation raised accuracy by more than 10%.
limits: Survey of reported numbers; the benchmarks differ and most are factual QA, not reasoning impasse.
agent_relevance: Gives a vocabulary: our S6 trigger is a context-memory or inter-context conflict between a produced output and a stated expectation.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without outside feedback, asking the model to review its answer does not help and often hurts. The model cannot tell by itself that its answer conflicts with the facts.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8% -> 38.1% after round 1 -> 41.8% round 2. GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 -> 75.1 -> 74.7. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0; GPT-4 CommonSenseQA 82.0 -> 79.5 -> 80.0. GPT-3.5 keeps its first answer 74.7% of the time on GSM8K.
limits: 2023-era models, 2 rounds, prompts from prior papers. Newer reasoning models trained for reflection may differ.
agent_relevance: Core support for G1/G2: do not trigger revision on a schedule or from opinion; trigger only on a real failing signal.

source: Huang et al. (2024) - oracle-label comparison
finding: Prior self-correction gains came from using the ground-truth label to decide when to stop. With oracle labels, self-correction looks strong; this is the conflict signal supplied from outside.
limits: Oracle is not available at test time; it shows the ceiling when a reliable conflict signal exists.
agent_relevance: The gain is in knowing when output conflicts with truth. Our tests and executable checks are the practical substitute for the oracle.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: Finding the mistake is the bottleneck. Given the mistake location, correction works and raises accuracy.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake, 5 tasks. GPT-4 best at mistake finding: only 52.87 overall accuracy with direct step-level prompting. Backtracking with true mistake location: gains on incorrect traces +18.04 to +43.92 points, losses on correct traces 0 to 11.43 points. Random location: gains only +5.16 to +20.39, losses 6.67 to 15.91.
limits: Traces sampled 85% incorrect / 15% correct; traces from PaLM 2; small classifier for location trained out of domain gave only modest gains.
agent_relevance: Code should locate the failing step (G2). Conflict detection that points to a place is worth far more than a general 'something is wrong'.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey
finding: No prior work shows reliable self-correction from prompted LLM feedback on general tasks. It works with reliable external feedback and with large-scale fine-tuning, and on tasks that decompose well.
numbers: Three conclusions: (1) no successful self-correction with prompted LLM feedback except in exceptionally suited tasks; (2) works with reliable external feedback; (3) fine-tuning enables it. Survey of many papers, no single N.
limits: Survey; judged mostly 2023-2024 work; unfair evaluations flagged (oracle labels, weak initial prompts).
agent_relevance: Confirms the schema choice: S6 conflict must come from an external check (code, test, retrieval), not model self-assessment.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: One irrelevant sentence causes large drops in math accuracy. Self-consistency and an instruction to ignore irrelevant text help.
numbers: Among problems the baseline solves, no more than 18% were solved consistently across all irrelevant-context types. With self-consistency (20 samples) recall of the correct answer reached 99.7%. Tested Codex (code-davinci-002) and GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003).
limits: Old models; instruction and exemplar fixes help only partly.
agent_relevance: Clashing or irrelevant information is not automatically ignored. Sample many, then let code select (G5), because the right answer is usually present among the samples.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: An agent loop that fires a reflection only when a simple failure signal appears (binary reward or a repeated-action heuristic) and stores the reflection as memory improves strongly.
numbers: ALFWorld 134 tasks: ReAct + Reflexion completed 130/134 with a heuristic for hallucination and inefficient planning; ReAct-only progress stalled between trials 6 and 7. HumanEval pass@1 91%. Reported +22% ALFWorld, +20% HotPotQA, +11% HumanEval over baselines.
limits: Code tasks use ground-truth tests; the heuristic is task-specific; GPT-3 era LLM in ALFWorld.
agent_relevance: Direct precedent for S6: a coded conflict trigger starts the reframe and the reflection is stored. Matches G1.

source: d'Aliberti and Horta Ribeiro (2026) The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models
finding: Spontaneous mid-trace 'Wait, let's re-evaluate' shifts are rare and mostly do not improve accuracy. They signal unstable inference, not insight.
numbers: 1M+ traces, hundreds of checkpoints, three domains (MATH-500, crosswords, Rush Hour). Shifts in about 6.31% of traces overall (about 7.6% for Qwen2.5-1.5B). Qwen2.5-1.5B accuracy 2.57% with shift vs 16.44% without. DeepSeek-R1 shift rate 0.00-0.25%, GPT-4o 0.88-2.21% on MATH-500.
limits: RL-tuned small models (Qwen2.5, Llama 3.1-8B) with a cue-based shift detector; external models checked on MATH-500 only.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on the model to notice impasse by itself (G1). A shift is not evidence of progress; verify after it.

source: d'Aliberti and Horta Ribeiro (2026) - entropy-gated external reconsideration
finding: Forcing a reconsideration step from outside, only when the model is uncertain (high token entropy), improves accuracy. Unconditional shifts do not.
numbers: Entropy gate: top 20% sequence entropy within domain. MATH-500 accuracy 0.322 -> 0.406 (+8.41 pp) with a Pass 2 reconsideration cue; smaller gains on crosswords and Rush Hour. Spontaneous shifts under high entropy still raw -7.40 pp, under low entropy -22.88 pp (Xwords).
limits: Needs token entropy access; small open models; fixed cue sentence.
agent_relevance: A coded uncertainty gate for S6 is supported. Where entropy is not visible, use disagreement across samples or check failure as the gate.

source: Building Effective AI Coding Agents for the Terminal (2026) - doom-loop detection
finding: A production coding-agent harness detects stuck loops in code: it hashes each tool call and pauses when the same call repeats. It also injects system reminders to steer long runs.
numbers: Algorithm 1: md5 fingerprint of tool name and args; deque window 20; pause when same fingerprint count >= 3. Config: doom-loop threshold 3 repeats, window 20 calls.
limits: Design description; no measured gain from this one detector in the text I read. Detects repetition, not conflict with expected output.
agent_relevance: A cheap coded impasse detector (repeat count) can be the first S6 trigger; add output-vs-expectation mismatch as the second.

source: Naeini et al. (2023) OCW - in-context examples and prompting limits
finding: More few-shot examples did not improve the grouping task. Examples with similar-looking words may themselves act as red herrings. Common errors were format errors and invented clues.
numbers: GPT-4 correct groups: 0-shot 239, 1-shot 262, 3-shot 272, 5-shot 269, 10-shot 249. Misformatted outputs 4.4% of predicted groups; hallucinated clues 6.6%; clues put inside connection 8.2%.
limits: Authors did not test chain of thought or tree of thoughts here; GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Prompt exemplars can induce fixation. In S6, show a new framing request without repeating the failed frame.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) NazoNazo - model scale vs date and benchmark design
finding: Parameter count did not predict insight accuracy; release date and training design did. Model scores are skewed low with most items very hard, unlike the bell-shaped human item difficulty.
numbers: Human scores bimodal (all-or-nothing) on 120 items (n=126). Item-level difficulty for LLMs: most items extremely low accuracy.
limits: Observational across 38 different models, confounded.
agent_relevance: Gains on impasse tasks come from process and training design, which a scaffold can mimic, not from size.

source: Kim et al. (2025) M-ARC - overconfidence and failure types
finding: Models answer pattern-matched even when the question shows an obvious contradiction, and keep high confidence. Self-consistency based confidence is overconfident.
numbers: Agreement-based and entropy-based Brier scores: top models (o1, Gemini Pro, Claude Opus, Llama 3.1 70B) overconfident despite low accuracy; larger models better calibrated than smaller. Specialised medical models (Medalpaca, Meditron) showed tangential reasoning and near-chance scores.
limits: Brier results shown in figures; exact scores in supplement not read.
agent_relevance: Agreement among samples is not a conflict signal when all samples share the same pattern (G4).

source: Xie et al. (2024) Stubborn Sloth - evidence order and popularity
finding: Models cling to memory more on popular facts, and the order of conflicting evidence changes the winner. Larger models resist incoherent counter-evidence more.
numbers: GPT-4 memory-answer ratio about 80% on most popular question group. Order sensitivity above 5% in most models, above 30% for PaLM2 and Llama2-7B.
limits: Factual QA; popularity measured by entity frequency.
agent_relevance: Randomise or fix the order of conflicting items in S6 and test both orders in code.

source: Huang et al. (2024) - why intrinsic self-correction flips right answers to wrong
finding: The model changes a correct answer to a wrong one more often than the reverse when told to review. The cause: it cannot judge its own reasoning, and a review prompt implies there is an error.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5: 74.7% of answers unchanged; of the changes, correct-to-wrong exceeded wrong-to-correct. CommonSenseQA: high rate of correct-to-incorrect changes since distractor options look relevant. GPT-4 and GPT-4-Turbo more likely to retain answers.
limits: Figure-based values; only retention rate quoted in text.
agent_relevance: A review step is a conflict-creating prompt. Run it only after a real failing signal.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) - fair-evaluation checklist for self-correction
finding: Many positive self-correction results use oracle information, weak first prompts, or unfair comparisons. Honest tests must separate feedback source (self, tool, retrieved knowledge) from refinement.
numbers: Three-stage frame: initial response, feedback, refinement; tables compare in-context, external tool/knowledge, and fine-tuning settings.
limits: Survey; judgement of fairness is the authors'.
agent_relevance: Use as the test design for our own benchmark of S6: report the feedback source and the no-feedback control.

source: Tyen et al. (2024) - mistake finding by task
finding: Even in clear, objective tasks, models are poor at spotting where their reasoning went wrong. Smaller models are worse; GPT-4 is best but far from reliable.
numbers: Mistake-finding accuracy rows seen: logical deduction GPT-4 40.67 / GPT-4-Turbo 21.33 (direct trace); PaLM 2 Unicorn 18.00; GPT-3.5-Turbo 10.10 on one task; Gemini Pro 37.67. GPT-4 overall 52.87.
limits: Table columns (trace, step, mistake prompting) were hard to separate in extracted text; per-cell attribution uncertain.
agent_relevance: Do not expect a model critic to localise the conflict. Use code that diffs output against the expectation.

source: Shi et al. (2023) GSM-IC - mitigations
finding: Adding irrelevant text to the exemplars, or a 'feel free to ignore irrelevant information' instruction, consistently raised accuracy. Models can partly learn to ignore by example or instruction.
numbers: Instruction text: 'Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions.' Reported as consistent gains across prompts; self-consistency raised all prompting methods.
quote: Feel free to ignore irrelevant information given in the questions.
limits: Only partial recovery; exact per-prompt accuracies not extracted.
agent_relevance: A single scaffold line naming the kind of clash can move behaviour a bit; code selection (self-consistency) moves it more.
